body.statement: For nuisance sequences with \(\eta_{NT}\to\eta\), uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\) and every finite \(M\), \(\sup_{|x|\le M}|(\sigma^2T)^{-1}[Q_F(\gamma+\sigma x/\sqrt m)-Q_F(\gamma)]-[\Phi_{NT,h}(x)-\Phi_{NT,h}(0)]|\xrightarrow{p}0\). Moreover, \(\widehat x_F=O_p(1)\) uniformly and \(\operatorname{dist}\{\widehat x_F,\mathcal S_{NT}(h)\}\xrightarrow{p}0\). Here \(h=\theta/\sigma\in[-\overline h,\overline h]\); no stochastic assertion is made for unbounded \(h\) or a genuine limiting tie.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(U_0=\operatorname{col}(\Lambda)\) and \(V_0=\operatorname{col}(F)\).  The two Gram-envelope assumptions imply that these spaces have dimension \(r\) and that
\[
s_r\!\left(\frac{\Lambda F^{\top}}{\sigma\sqrt T}\right)
 \geq \frac{\sqrt{N\underline\lambda}\sqrt{T\underline f}}
 {\overline\sigma\sqrt T}
 \geq C_0\sqrt m                                             \tag{1}
\]
for \(C_0=\sqrt{\underline\lambda\underline f}/\overline\sigma>0\).  All remaining constants below can be chosen uniformly on a fixed compact subset of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\).

The supported vectors admit the orthonormal decompositions
\[
e_1=\frac d{\sqrt{n_1}},\qquad
e_2=\frac{a_S-\mu_{a,N}d}{\sqrt{n_1v_{a,N}}},\qquad
f_1=\frac{qvec}{\sqrt{t_1}},\qquad
f_2=\frac{b_S-\mu_{b,T}qvec}{\sqrt{t_1v_{b,T}}}.              \tag{2}
\]
The finite supported-variance envelope makes every denominator in (2) positive.  The four exact orthogonality assumptions give \(e_1,e_2\in U_0^\perp\) and \(f_1,f_2\in V_0^\perp\).  For \(\beta=\gamma+\sigma x/\sqrt m\), define
\[
P_x=\frac{H-(\beta-\gamma)D}{\sigma\sqrt T}.
\]
Substitution of the definitions of \(H,D,\delta\), and the four vectors in (2) gives the exact identity
\[
P_x=(e_1,e_2)B_{NT,h}(x)(f_1,f_2)^{\top}.                    \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, the common scalar multiplying the heterogeneous part is
\[
\frac{\theta\sqrt{n_1t_1}}{\sigma\sqrt{mT}}
=h\sqrt{\frac Nm}\sqrt{p_Nq_T}=h\kappa_{NT},
\]
and the scalar multiplying the coefficient displacement is \(x\kappa_{NT}\).  Thus (3) also verifies the rectangular normalization in the claimed profile.

Complete orthonormal bases beginning with bases of \(U_0\) and \(V_0\).  Gaussian orthogonal invariance and (3) yield
\[
\frac{Y-\beta D}{\sigma\sqrt T}
=\begin{pmatrix}G+Z_{11}&Z_{12}\\Z_{21}&Z_{22}+P_x\end{pmatrix},              \tag{4}
\]
where \(s_r(G)\geq C_0\sqrt m\), every entry of \(Z=(Z_{jk})\) is independent \(\mathcal N(0,1/T)\), and the nonzero block of \(P_x\) has the two-by-two representation in (3).  The cited rectangular Gaussian outlier result, applied with zero perturbation, also gives \(\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_p(1)\).  Hence, uniformly for \(|x|\leq M\), the lower blocks of every unit singular vector belonging to one of the first \(r\) singular values in (4) have norm \(O_p(m^{-1/2})\).  This follows directly from the two lower block equations for a singular pair: their left sides have singular value at least \(C_0\sqrt m-O_p(1)\), whereas all off-diagonal blocks have bounded operator norm.

For completeness, interpolate from \(P_0\) to \(P_x\).  At differentiability points, the derivative of the sum of the first \(r\) squared singular values is twice the Frobenius inner product of the perturbation with the lower-right block of the corresponding rank-\(r\) truncated singular-value expansion.  By the preceding lower-block bounds, that lower-right block is \(O_p(m^{-1/2})\).  The sum of squared singular values is locally Lipschitz, so integration across the finitely many nondifferentiability points gives
\[
\sup_{|x|\leq M}\left|
\sum_{j=1}^{r}s_j(G+Z+P_x)^2-\sum_{j=1}^{r}s_j(G+Z+P_0)^2
\right|=o_p(1).                                               \tag{5}
\]
Applying the same block equations to the symmetric dilation of (4), and eliminating the coordinates in the strong block, gives a Schur-complement error bounded by
\(C\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2/s_r(G)\).  Therefore
\[
\sup_{|x|\leq M}\left|s_{r+1}(G+Z+P_x)-s_1(Z_{22}+P_x)\right|=o_p(1).          \tag{6}
\]
Equations (5)--(6) are uniform because \(P_x\) ranges over a compact set and the lower bound in (1) is uniform.

We next record why the cited pointwise outlier theorem is sufficient here.  For any compact collection of deterministic two-by-two matrices, take a finite Frobenius \(\epsilon\)-net.  Gaussian invariance makes the law depend only on the singular values of the perturbation.  Weyl's inequality gives
\[
|s_1(Z_{22}+P)-s_1(Z_{22}+\widetilde P)|\leq\|P-\widetilde P\|_F.             \tag{7}
\]
The noise operator norm is tight, and \((\rho,s)\mapsto\psi_\rho(s)\) is continuous at the spectral edge because the two displayed branches agree when \(s=\rho^{1/4}\).  The finite net, (7), and then \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) upgrade the cited convergence to uniform convergence over the compact collection.  If \(c>1\), apply the cited result to \(c^{-1/2}(Z_{22}+P_x)^{\top}\), whose aspect ratio tends to \(1/c\); multiplying the resulting squared singular value by \(c\) gives exactly
\[
\psi_c(s)=
\begin{cases}
(1+\sqrt c)^2,&s\leq c^{1/4},\\
s^2+1+c+c/s^2,&s>c^{1/4}.
\end{cases}                                                     \tag{8}
\]
Replacing \((N,T)\) by \((N-r,T-r)\), and variance \(1/(T-r)\) by \(1/T\), changes (8) by \(o(1)\).  A subsequence contradiction, using compactness of the nuisance set, proves the same assertion uniformly when \(c_N\), rather than a fixed \(c\), varies in the maintained aspect envelope.  Consequently,
\[
\sup_{|x|\leq M}\left|s_1(Z_{22}+P_x)^2-\psi_{c_N}\{s_1(B_{NT,h}(x))\}\right|
\xrightarrow{p}0.                                               \tag{9}
\]

The Frobenius part has no omitted term.  Orthogonality of \(P_x\) to the strong block gives
\[
\left\|\frac{Y-\beta D}{\sigma\sqrt T}\right\|_F^2
-\left\|\frac{Y-\gamma D}{\sigma\sqrt T}\right\|_F^2
=\|B_{NT,h}(x)\|_F^2-\|B_{NT,h}(0)\|_F^2
+2\langle Z,P_x-P_0\rangle_F.                                  \tag{10}
\]
The last term is affine in \(x\), has mean zero, and on \(|x|\leq M\) has variance bounded by \(C_M/T\); hence its supremum is \(o_p(1)\).  The exact profile identity in \(\mathrm{def{:}full\mbox{-}profile}\), followed by (5), (6), (9), and (10), proves the asserted compact-profile convergence.

It remains to justify that a minimizer cannot escape the compact coordinate sets on which this convergence was established.  Write
\[
R=\kappa^2h^2(\mu_a^2+v_a)(\mu_b^2+v_b),\qquad
L_\infty=\kappa^2h^2v_av_b-(1+c).                               \tag{11}
\]
At \(x=0\), the matrix \(B_{\eta,h}(0)\) has rank one and squared singular value \(R\).  If \(R\leq\sqrt c\), then
\[
L_\infty-\Phi_{\eta,h}(0)
=2\sqrt c-\kappa^2h^2(\mu_a^2v_b+v_a\mu_b^2)\geq\sqrt c.       \tag{12}
\]
If \(R>\sqrt c\), then
\[
L_\infty-\Phi_{\eta,h}(0)=\kappa^2h^2v_av_b+c/R>0.             \tag{13}
\]
The right sides of (12)--(13) have a positive infimum on the maintained compact nuisance-signal set: in the second case use \(c\geq\underline c\) and the finite upper bound on \(R\).

To identify the tail, let \(e=e_1\), \(f=f_1\), and write the lower block as \(-t ef^{\top}+A\), where \(|t|=\kappa_{NT}|x|\) and \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_p(1)\).  Direct second-order expansion of the top eigenvalue of \((-t ef^{\top}+A)(-t ef^{\top}+A)^{\top}\) gives
\[
s_1(-t ef^{\top}+A)^2
=t^2-2t\,e^{\top}Af+\|A^{\top}e\|_2^2
+\|(I-ee^{\top})Af\|_2^2+O_p(|t|^{-1}).                        \tag{14}
\]
The remainder is uniform once \(|t|\) exceeds a fixed constant because \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_p(1)\).  For the Gaussian part of \(A\), the two quadratic terms in (14) converge to \(1\) and \(c\), respectively; their cross terms with the bounded deterministic spike converge to zero.  After cancellation with the Frobenius terms in (10), the deterministic remainder is
\[
\|(I-ee^{\top})P_0(I-ff^{\top})\|_F^2-(1+c)
=\kappa^2h^2v_av_b-(1+c)=L_\infty.                              \tag{15}
\]
The same expansion applied to the joint \((r+1)\)-dimensional diverging block covers sequences with \(|x|\) comparable to \(\sqrt m\); exact two-sided orthogonality makes the baseline and treatment blocks orthogonal before adding noise.  Thus every sequence \(|x_{NT}|\to\infty\) allowed by \(\gamma+\sigma x_{NT}/\sqrt m\in\mathcal B\) has profiled objective, relative to the common terms, converging to (15).  Equations (12)--(15) yield constants \(M_0<\infty\) and \(\epsilon_0>0\), uniform on the compact parameter set, such that with probability tending to one every global minimizer lies in \([-M_0,M_0]\).

On this last compact interval, the proved uniform criterion convergence applies.  By the definition of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{stab}}\), every limiting criterion has a unique minimizer and a positive separation outside each neighborhood of it.  Compactness upgrades this to a common separation modulus.  Since \(\eta_{NT}\to\eta\) and \(\Phi_{NT,h}\to\Phi_{\eta,h}\) uniformly on compacts, the deterministic sets \(\mathcal S_{NT}(h)\) lie in that neighborhood as well.  The standard contradiction proof of the argmin lemma now uses only the displayed separation: if \(\operatorname{dist}\{\widehat x_F,\mathcal S_{NT}(h)\}\geq\epsilon\), the deterministic criterion gap is bounded below while the stochastic sup-norm error tends to zero.  This is impossible with probability bounded away from zero.  It proves both the distance assertion and uniform \(O_p(1)\) localization.  A genuine limiting tie lacks the required separation, which is exactly why it is excluded from the conclusion.
body.justification: This is the bridge from fixed-spike random-matrix theory to the coefficient chosen by the actual full-sample IFE objective on a bounded local experiment.
body.gap: Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi (2012) give fixed-spike limits; Bai (2009) does not cover a noise-scale treatment factor or uniform coefficient-indexed spectral localization.
body.consumer: It supplies the limit experiment needed to determine whether whole-sample profiling can absorb local low-rank heterogeneity even after ordinary baseline-confounding terms are removed by assumption.
